record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Cosmic censorship for rotating supersymmetric configurations
record.original_question: In classical supergravity, Bogomol'nyi bounds do not include angular momentum, so supersymmetric or B-bound-saturating rotating configurations can still have naked singularities. What principle should enforce cosmic censorship for such rotating configurations, and can string theory's microscopic rules for building states prevent angular momentum from producing naked singularities while preserving the correct extremality bound?

evidence.quote: In N = 2 the extreme and supersymmetric limits in presence of angular momentum are even more different. The situation is essentially the same but now M → |Q + iP| (we stress that J does never appear in the B bound) is always beyond the extremality limit and produces naked singularities.

We have seen that (classical) SUSY seems to act as a cosmic censor in general only in static situations. Solutions that saturate the B bound and have angular momentum have naked singularities but are allowed by SUSY.

With respect to the angular momentum problem, at least, this seems to be a success of string theory. In SUGRA, if we start with an ERN BH, the rules seem to allow us to add angular momentum while keeping the B bound saturated (by diminishing the mass). This is not possible in string theory [30] where it seems that we can only add angular momentum by adding fermions increasing at the same time the mass so the B bound is no longer saturated but the extremality bound is exactly saturated and never trespassed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider four-dimensional N=2 supergravity coupled to vector multiplets, and the family of stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat black-hole-type solutions characterized by mass M, electric charge Q, magnetic charge P, and angular momentum J. The Bogomol'nyi (BPS) bound takes the form M ≥ |Q + iP| and does not involve J, while the extremality (no-naked-singularity) bound is more restrictive once J ≠ 0: an extreme Reissner–Nordström-like configuration saturating M = |Q + iP| but carrying nonzero angular momentum lies beyond its extremality limit and exhibits naked singularities, yet is still permitted by the supersymmetry algebra.

(a) Identify a general principle, intrinsic to classical (super)gravity, that would enforce cosmic censorship for such stationary rotating BPS-saturating configurations, ruling out those with naked singularities even though they saturate the Bogomol'nyi bound.

(b) Determine whether the microscopic counting/state-building rules of string theory (for instance, the requirement that angular momentum be added only by exciting fermionic degrees of freedom, which simultaneously increase the mass) can be shown, in full generality, to (i) forbid configurations with J ≠ 0 that saturate M = |Q + iP|, and (ii) instead force exact saturation of the appropriate extremality bound that includes J, so that the extremality bound is never exceeded.

Provide either a proof of such a principle and a matching microscopic derivation, or a counterexample.
artifact.category_tag: Supersymmetric black holes and cosmic censorship
artifact.status_search_result: The question of why angular momentum must respect the extremality (rather than just the BPS) bound, and a general gravitational principle enforcing cosmic censorship for rotating supersymmetric configurations, remains an open conceptual problem. Partial results in N=2 supergravity show that requiring unbroken supersymmetry globally excludes many naked-singularity sources, but everywhere-supersymmetric rotating solutions with pathologies still exist. Microscopic string-theory arguments (fermion-induced angular momentum increasing the mass) are known in specific setups but no general theorem is established.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetry and cosmic censorship
status_evidence.snippet: Requiring unbroken supersymmetry in N=2, d=4 supergravity ensures in most cases the absence of naked singularities, though everywhere-supersymmetric solutions with global angular momentum and nontrivial scalar fields exist.
status_evidence.claim: A general principle enforcing cosmic censorship for rotating BPS configurations is not established; only partial results under global supersymmetry are known.

status_evidence.title: Extremal black hole - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: An extremal black hole has the minimum mass compatible with its charge and angular momentum; in supersymmetric theories extremal black holes are often BPS.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between BPS saturation and the J-dependent extremality bound is theory-specific and not derived from a single universal principle.
